current_answer: Selective value creation, with a supported vulnerability to excessive or incompatible expectations—not a demonstrated, uniformly overpriced AI sector. Paid customer use, provider cash, useful older capacity, investor realizations and workable financing are substantive favorable evidence. The new NVIDIA and Freshworks ownership tests find plausible costed paths, not proof that either selected security is a bubble. The customer-funding comparison shows that the current build was funded; repeating it still requires adequate net customer cash, feasible investment and finance on supportable terms. A profitable supplier does not establish its buyers’ returns. An earlier seller’s cash does not validate the next owner’s price. Ownership judgment; repeat-purchase judgment.
summary: AI’s commercial expansion is real. Whether a particular investment is well priced—and whether customers can fund the next purchase—are harder, separate questions.
uncertainty: For capital recycling, match the cash actually received to the recipient’s complete costs, retained claim and subsequent funding obligations. Successful post-completion collections and manageable future claims would strengthen the productive account; demonstrably unfunded required uses or poor comparable entry economics would weaken it. Neither a new issue price nor one early exit settles the question. Evidence that would distinguish these paths.

June/July accounts, earlier contracts and historical transactions are not October cash balances. All earlier evidence boundaries.
